Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live''

Indian Standard 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



SPECIFICATION FOR 
SYRINGE, WATER, SELF-FILLING, DENTAL 



U Scope— Dimensions and other requirements for self-filling water syringe used in dentistry. 



2* Shape and Dimensions — As shown In Fig. I. 
3. Material 

Components 
Barrel 

Spring 

All other components 



Material 



Brass tube, Alloy No. I of 15:407-1966 
'Specification for brass tubes for 
general purposes {second revision) ' 

Stainless steel wire of Section V of 
IS: 4454- 1 967 'Specification for steel 
wires for cold formed springs ' 

Brass rod. Designation CuZnBO of 
IS:4I70-I967 'Specification for brass 
rods for general engineering purposes ' 



4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The barrel and plunger assembly shall be concentric. Plunger shall be removable from the barrel to 
facilitate cleaning. 

4.2 Barrel, plunger, piston and nozzle shall have fine smooth ground finish, free from pits, hair lines, high 
spots and grind marks. 

4.3 Piston movement inside the barrel shall be smooth, even and jerk-free. 

4.4 The external surfaces of syringe shall be plated chromium over nickel and the plating shall conform to 
Service Grade No. 3 of IS: 4827- 1 968 'Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on 
copper and copper alloys'. 

5. Tests 

5.1 Suck water Into syringe. Hold the filled syringe vertical with nozzle upwards. Push the plunger up. 
No air shall be ejected and the water shall emerge from the syringe In a jet, 

5.2 The syringe shall be kept vertically with thumb rest on the top of a compression-type springe balance. 
The force required to push the plunger completely in the barrel shall be 26*97 ±2*45 N (27Sdb0'25 kgf). 

5.3 Suck the water into the syringe and hold it horizontally. Force out the water applying full force on 
the plunger. The jet of water from the nozzle shall cover a distance of not less than 4 metres. There 
shall be no leakage past the piston. 

5.4 Seal the nozzie end of the syringe after sucking In water. Apply 49 N (5 kgf) axial force on the 
plunger to compress water inside the barrel. No water shall leak through the nozzle-barrel joint and 
past the piston. 

6. Marking— The syringe shall be marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark and the 
country of manufacture. 

6.1 ISI Certification Mark/ng — Details available from the Indian Standards Institution, New Delhi I. 

7. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



Adopted 22 September 1972 



March 1973, ISI
